response.sql: WITH state_counts AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(p.death_state, ''), 'missing') AS state, COUNT(DISTINCT h.player_id) AS cnt FROM hall_of_fame h JOIN player p ON p.player_id = h.player_id GROUP BY 1), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM state_counts), above AS (SELECT s.cnt FROM state_counts s CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE s.cnt > o.avg_cnt) SELECT AVG(a.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(a.cnt - o.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM above a CROSS JOIN overall o;

assumptions.assumption: The inner join to player drops Hall of Fame rows whose player_id has no match in player, as the request specifies.
A missing death_state is either NULL or an empty string; both are grouped together under the label 'missing'.
The missing-state group counts as one of the states when computing the overall average count and the threshold.

alternatives.interpretation: The missing-state group is excluded from the states entirely, so the overall average and the above-average filter use only states with a recorded death_state.
alternatives.sql: WITH state_counts AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(p.death_state, ''), 'missing') AS state, COUNT(DISTINCT h.player_id) AS cnt FROM hall_of_fame h JOIN player p ON p.player_id = h.player_id GROUP BY 1), named AS (SELECT state, cnt FROM state_counts WHERE state <> 'missing'), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM named), above AS (SELECT s.cnt FROM named s CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE s.cnt > o.avg_cnt) SELECT AVG(a.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(a.cnt - o.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM above a CROSS JOIN overall o;
